name: docket
description: Projects, tickets, time and budgets for agencies: see your week, book time, work on tickets.

interface.longDescription:
docket is project, ticket and time management for agencies. Connect your docket workspace to ask about your work and act on it in plain language.

See your week: which tickets are due or planned, how many hours you have booked against your working time, and what is new in your notifications.

Book time: log time on a ticket, start, pause and book stopwatches, and correct or delete your own entries.

Work on tickets: create a ticket, comment on it, move its dates, close it or reopen it. Tickets mirrored from Jira stay read-only and are changed in Jira.

Keep an eye on projects: search projects, tickets and customers, check project budgets and team capacity, and, where your role in docket allows it, look at invoices, quotations, the financial summary and the revenue forecast.

Everything respects your permissions in docket. You only ever see what you can see in the app, and you only book, change and delete your own time. You sign in with your docket account and choose your workspace; an admin can turn AI connections off for the whole workspace, and you can disconnect at any time in your docket profile.

positive.description: See what is on the user's plate this week
positive.prompt: Which tickets are on my plate this week?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the user's open tickets that are overdue or due this week, each with its project and due date; overdue ones are marked as such. Read-only, no confirmation needed.

positive.description: Compare booked hours with the user's working time
positive.prompt: How many hours have I booked this week compared to my working time?
positive.expected_behavior: Shows the hours booked per day this week against the user's working time, the total, and the days with gaps. Read-only.

positive.description: Book time on one of the user's tickets
positive.prompt: Log 1 hour for today on my first ticket due this week, description: Design review.
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the user's tickets due this week, asks for confirmation, then creates a 60-minute time entry for today on the first of them with the description 'Design review' and the user's default service, and reports the ticket and project it was booked on.

positive.description: Create a ticket and comment on it
positive.prompt: On the Rebrand & Design System project, create a ticket 'Prepare client workshop' due next Friday and add the comment 'Agenda draft follows tomorrow.'
positive.expected_behavior: Finds the project, asks for confirmation, creates the ticket assigned to the user with next Friday as due date, adds the comment, and links or names the new ticket.

positive.prompt: Show the budgets of my running projects. Which ones are over budget?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the running projects with budget, amount used and percentage, and names those above 100 % (or says that none are). Read-only.

negative.description: Parcel tracking is not time tracking: docket should not be called.
A general time question has nothing to do with the user's work in docket.
negative.prompt: What time is it in Tokyo right now?

negative.description: Writing a generic template needs no data from docket and must not create anything there.
negative.prompt: Write a project plan template for a website relaunch.

publication.release_notes: Initial release: see your week and tickets, book time and run stopwatches, create, comment, reschedule, close and reopen tickets, check budgets, capacity and (by role) invoices, quotations and forecasts.
